title: How to do Horizontal Yo-Yo Tricks [Like a Pro] - Trapeze / Pinwheel / Bind

segments.text: This is a horizontal yo-yo trick combo.
Horizontal tricks are very important
technique in modern 1A yo-yo play.
However, they can also be quite
challenging at first.
>> In this video, I will explain the basics
and the best way to practice for players
new to horizontal tricks.
>> I will explain step by step from step
one to step five. Please choose the
steps to work on based on your level.
>> First, let's learn how to throw
diagonally.
>> This applies to all the following steps,
too. But, at first, diagonal is okay.
Going straight to horizontal is very
difficult. Gradually [music] adjust the
angle and aim for horizontal. If you
want to make it horizontal, throw by
aiming more diagonally [music]
upward than you think you need to. I
recommend using a less responsive yo-yo
at first to get the right feel.
If you don't have one, start from step
two using an unresponsive yo-yo. If you
have mastered lasso or UFO, you can
progress through the next steps more
efficiently. Be sure to keep that in
mind.
>> If you are finding it difficult to throw
diagonally, here is a tip.
>> Just like this, unwind a short length of
string from the yo-yo. Hold the yo-yo
horizontally with your non-dominant
hand, hook the string onto your dominant
hand's index [music] finger, and try
throwing it slightly diagonally upward.
This is good practice for controlling
the yo-yo horizontally.
Let's try doing a pinwheel by keeping
the string between your thumb and index
finger. This will help you practice
moving the yo-yo horizontally.
It's okay even if it's at an angle at
first. Try to maintain the pinwheel
state.
A slightly shorter string is recommended
for both responsive and unresponsive
yo-yos. Until you get used to it, a
longer string can be difficult to
control.
Let's try trapeze in the horizontal
state. It will be difficult to hit the
string directly at first. Let's try
hitting a trapeze after doing a pinwheel
[music] once.
Once you can do a trapeze, [music] try a
somersault.
After doing a trapeze, keep the yo-yo
rotating with the momentum you already
have.
It's okay if at this stage you can't
catch it yet. I will explain how to bind
in the next step.
Let's try doing a
bind. Just like steps 1, 2, and 3, it's
okay to start at a diagonal angle
instead of exactly horizontal.
After doing a trapeze,
do reverse trapeze with your middle
finger and do a bind.
>> [music]
>> I also recommend adding a reverse
somersault because it builds the yo-yo's
momentum. This might make it easier.
>> [music]
>> If you are finding binding to be
difficult, here is a little trick. By
doing a jail, you can take the yo-yo
from a horizontal state to a vertical
state.
>> [music]
>> Once you have mastered horizontal
trapeze and bind, try some tricks. I I
introduce a few, so please try the one
that seems achievable.
>> [music]
[music]
>> I recommend using yo-yos that have a
wide radius and low edge. This is
because they make it easier to shoot the
sling and control the angle. If you've
already mastered the finger spin and
DNA, try connecting into them from
horizontal trick combos.
Yo-yo used in this video is Silk by
General Yo-yo Design. Also, please check
the description box for my recommended
yo-yos. If you found this video helpful,
please give me a like and comment and
don't forget to subscribe. See you in
the next tutorial.
